# Small Omega

Small Omega (╧ë) notation is used to describe a lower bound on the growth rate of a function. Specifically, it indicates that a function _g(n)_ grows strictly slower than another function _f(n)_ as _n_ approaches infinity. This means that for any constant _c > 0_, there exists a value _nΓéÇ_ such that _g(n) < c_f(n)\* for all _n > nΓéÇ_. In simpler terms, _f(n)_ is a strict lower bound for _g(n)_.
